title: Behavioral Core
description: Role-neutral behavioral prompts tagged by competency and seniority, with CARL coaching hooks.

questions.title: Starting From a Blank Page
questions.prompt: Tell me about a time you took on a problem nobody had defined yet and turned it into something real.
follow_ups: Which assumptions did you check first, and which turned out to be wrong?
Where did you cut scope so you could deliver something real instead of over-building?
What would you do differently if you started over today?
questions.carl_focus: Make your own framing of the problem crisp, show the trade-offs you weighed, and close with something you learned and still use.

questions.title: Fixing a Problem Outside Your Lane
questions.prompt: Describe a time you noticed a problem outside your own responsibilities and decided to own fixing it.
follow_ups: How did you earn buy-in from the people who were responsible for that area?
What did you have to set aside or negotiate to make time for it?
questions.carl_focus: Explain why you stepped in rather than escalating, and show how the fix lasted after you moved on.

questions.title: Aligning Groups With Competing Priorities
questions.prompt: Tell me about a time you needed people outside your team to agree on a direction when they had competing priorities.
follow_ups: What was the strongest objection, and how did you address it?
Did you change part of your proposal based on their feedback?
questions.carl_focus: Show that you understood the other group's constraints before explaining how you built agreement.

questions.title: Changing a Decision With Evidence
questions.prompt: Describe a time you convinced a manager or a senior stakeholder to change course using evidence.
follow_ups: What made the evidence strong enough to shift a plan people had already committed to?
What did switching late cost, and how did you reduce that risk?
questions.carl_focus: Pair the moment the evidence landed with the concrete outcome for the business or the people you serve.

questions.title: Disagreeing With a Colleague
questions.prompt: Tell me about a strong disagreement you had with a colleague or someone more senior. How did you work through it?
follow_ups: Looking back, which parts of their argument were right?
How was the working relationship after the decision was made?
questions.carl_focus: Avoid casting the other person as the villain. Strong answers show curiosity, clear criteria for deciding, and commitment once the call is made.

questions.title: Pushing Back on a Deadline or Request
questions.prompt: Tell me about a time you pushed back on a request or an aggressive deadline because you were worried about quality, safety, or risk.
follow_ups: What alternative did you propose instead of just saying no?
How did you describe the risk in terms the other person cared about?
questions.carl_focus: Show the concrete options and trade-offs you offered rather than a flat refusal.

questions.title: A Mistake You Owned
questions.prompt: Walk me through a meaningful mistake you made at work. What happened, and what changed afterward?
follow_ups: What was the earliest warning sign you missed?
What did you put in place so a colleague could not make the same mistake?
questions.carl_focus: Own the mistake directly without deflecting, then spend about half your answer on what you learned and what you changed.

questions.title: A Bet That Didn't Pay Off
questions.prompt: Tell me about a project or idea you invested a lot in that didn't turn out the way you hoped.
follow_ups: How did you recognize it was time to change direction or stop?
How did you communicate that decision to the people affected?
questions.carl_focus: Show honesty about what went wrong and a clear lesson that changed how you scope later work.

questions.title: When Priorities Shifted Mid-Project
questions.prompt: Describe a time the requirements or priorities changed partway through a project. How did you adapt without losing momentum or quality?
follow_ups: How did you keep the people around you from being thrown off by the change?
Which earlier decisions made the change easier or harder?
questions.carl_focus: Explain how you decided what to do under uncertainty, not just the order of events.

questions.title: Deciding With Incomplete Information
questions.prompt: Tell me about an important decision you had to make with incomplete information and little time.
follow_ups: How did you tell apart the decisions you could reverse from the ones you couldn't?
What did you set up so you would know early if the decision was wrong?
questions.carl_focus: Emphasize how you limited the downside and what told you the decision was working.

questions.title: Raising the Standard
questions.prompt: Tell me about a time you raised the standard for the quality of work on your team.
follow_ups: How did you get people to adopt the standard willingly rather than seeing it as bureaucracy?
How did you know it was actually making the work better or faster?
questions.carl_focus: Ground the standard in a real pain point and show that people adopted it in a way you could observe or measure.

questions.title: A Root Cause That Surprised You
questions.prompt: Describe a difficult problem you investigated where the root cause surprised you.
follow_ups: What dead ends did you rule out along the way, and what finally revealed the answer?
How did you keep the problem from coming back?
questions.carl_focus: Walk through how you formed and tested each hypothesis so the interviewer hears structured judgment.

questions.title: Learning From the People You Serve
questions.prompt: Tell me about a time you worked directly with customers, users, or the people your work serves, and it changed what you delivered.
follow_ups: What would you have missed if you had only worked from the original brief?
How did you balance getting it right with getting it done on time?
questions.carl_focus: Connect what you learned from them to the specific changes you made and the difference it made.

questions.title: Simplifying Instead of Adding
questions.prompt: Describe a time you made a process, a product, or a way of working simpler instead of adding to it.
follow_ups: What resistance did you face when you proposed removing something?
How did you check that the people who relied on the old way were not hurt?
questions.carl_focus: Show judgment: why removing beat adding, and what changed for people afterward.

questions.title: Helping a Struggling Colleague
questions.prompt: Tell me about a time you helped a colleague who was struggling with important work.
follow_ups: How did you avoid simply doing the work for them?
What skills or habits did they carry into later work?
questions.carl_focus: Show how you worked out what was really holding them back and helped them grow instead of rescuing them.

questions.title: Giving Difficult Feedback
questions.prompt: Describe a time you gave difficult feedback to a colleague. How did you approach it?
follow_ups: How did you prepare so the feedback came across as specific and supportive rather than personal?
What changed after that conversation?
questions.carl_focus: Highlight care, specificity, and the follow-through you could observe.

questions.title: Your Most Complex Delivery
questions.prompt: Tell me about the most complex piece of work you have delivered from start to finish.
follow_ups: Which part carried the most risk, and how did you reduce it before it could hurt you?
How did you decide it was ready?
questions.carl_focus: Keep the setup to about 30 seconds so you have room for your hardest decisions and the real outcome.

questions.title: Taking a Shortcut on Purpose
questions.prompt: Tell me about a time you deliberately took a shortcut to hit an important deadline, and how you dealt with the consequences later.
follow_ups: How did you keep the shortcut from becoming the normal way of working?
Did you go back and fix it, or did it turn out not to matter?
questions.carl_focus: Pragmatic answers show the limits you set on purpose and honest hindsight.

questions.title: Driving a Long-Term Plan
questions.prompt: Describe a plan spanning several months or more that you came up with and drove across multiple teams.
follow_ups: How did you order the early wins so people saw value before the whole thing was finished?
Which parts of the original plan did you have to revise along the way?
questions.carl_focus: Explain the reasoning behind the plan, the order you did things in, and how you knew it was being adopted.

questions.title: Putting a New Tool or Method to Work
questions.prompt: Tell me about a time you evaluated a new tool, method, or technology and turned it into something your team could rely on.
follow_ups: How did you handle the ways it could fail so that people could trust it?
How did you judge whether it was better than what you had before?
questions.carl_focus: Highlight how you evaluated it, the safeguards you added, and what you learned about how it holds up in real use.
